Asked which deed is best, the Prophet named faith in Allah and His Messenger, then jihad in Allah's cause, then an accepted Hajj.
Praying on the Night of Qadr and Ramadan nights and fasting Ramadan with faith and hope bring forgiveness of past sins, and fighting in Allah's cause earns reward or Paradise.
Three earn double reward: a scripture follower who also believes in Muhammad, a slave true to Allah and master, and one who educates, frees and marries his slave woman.
Walking far to the mosque, waiting for the imam, removing a thorny branch, the Adhan, the first row and Isha and Fajr earn reward; five kinds of death are martyrdom.
No good deeds on other days surpass those of the first ten days of Dhul Hijja, not even jihad, unless one risks life and property and returns with neither.
Bilal, whose footsteps the Prophet heard ahead of him in Paradise, said his best deed was praying after every ablution, by day or night.
If people knew the reward of the call to prayer and the first row they would cast lots for them, and they would crawl to the Fajr and Isha prayers.
Fasting one day for Allah's pleasure keeps one's face seventy years from the Fire, and whoever spends two things in His cause is called by all Paradise's gatekeepers.
Three get a double reward: a man who teaches, frees and marries his slave girl, a Scripture believer who accepts the Prophet, and a faithful slave.
The best deeds are praying at the stated times, being dutiful to parents and jihad in Allah's Cause.
